speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, such as whether the spots are raised, flat, or fluid-filled? Also, have you noticed any new lesions appearing on your face, palms, or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. The progression from a facial rash sparing the perioral area to the trunk and extremities, following a mild prodrome, is quite characteristic. To help confirm the diagnosis, have you noticed if the rash on the trunk looks like "cherry-red" spots with pale centers, often described as a "dewdrop on a rose petal"?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a trunk and extremity rash after a mild prodrome is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum
